Let us first proves this for sheaves of sets.
Fix <MATH_0001> open. Pick <MATH_0002>.
We are going to construct an element
<MATH_0003>.
We can define a value <MATH_0004> in the stalk <MATH_0005>
for every <MATH_0006> by picking a <MATH_0007>
with <MATH_0008> and setting <MATH_0009>
equal to the equivalence class of <MATH_0010>
in the stalk. Clearly, the family <MATH_0011>
satisfies condition <MATH_0012> because the maps <MATH_0013>
for varying <MATH_0014>
are compatible with restrictions in the sheaf <MATH_0015>.
Thus, by the proof of Lemma <REF_0001>
we see that <MATH_0016> corresponds
to a unique element <MATH_0017> of <MATH_0018>.
Thus we have defined a set map
<MATH_0019>.
The compatibility between <MATH_0020> and <MATH_0021>
follows from Lemma <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
We leave it to the reader to show that the construction
of <MATH_0022> is compatible with restriction mappings as we vary
<MATH_0023>. Thus we may apply Lemma
<REF_0003> above to
``glue'' them to the desired <MATH_0024>-map.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Finally, we note that the map of sheaves of sets so constructed
satisfies the property that the map on stalks
<MATH_0025>
is the colimit of the system of maps <MATH_0026> as
<MATH_0027> varies over those elements that
contain <MATH_0028> and <MATH_0029> varies over those elements that
contain <MATH_0030>. In particular, if <MATH_0031> and <MATH_0032>
are the underlying sheaves of sets of sheaves of algebraic structures,
then we see that the maps on stalks is a morphism of algebraic
structures. Hence we conclude that the associated map of
sheaves of underlying sets <MATH_0033>
satisfies the assumptions of
Lemma <REF_0004>.
We conclude that <MATH_0034>
is a morphism of sheaves with values in <MATH_0035>.
And by adjointness this means that <MATH_0036> is
an <MATH_0037>-map of sheaves of algebraic structures.
